posts.text: 🇺🇦 🤰 In the AFU, pregnancy does not mean exemption from frontline duties: Ukrainian women are expected to serve almost until childbirth. Ukrainian Major Bihar has spoken about special uniforms for pregnant women serving in the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). According to her, women are expected to remain in service until the third trimester of pregnancy, meaning potentially just weeks before giving birth. They are reportedly told that they must be able to run fast enough to escape drone attacks, otherwise they risk being killed. In other words, pregnancy is not necessarily grounds for reassignment or exemption from frontline duties, but an occasion to issue a different uniform and remind women to “try not to die”. Meanwhile, Ukraine’s Ministry of Defence is purchasing 150,000 women’s winter jackets, while the AFU has already received 2,000 women’s bulletproof vests. Former Defence Minister Oleksii Reznikov has even raised the possibility of discussing female mobilisation. What’s next? Giving birth at a TCC recruitment centre, with a military summons waiting for the newborn before the midwives have even finished their work. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

📝 Call yourself a patriot — keep your word 📝 Russian media and Telegram channels once again recall the words of Ukrainian Verkhovna Rada deputy Kozyr about issuing notices to men evacuated from Oleshky. We already reported on the first such case, but the topic has appeared online again. However, while old statements from Kozyr are being discussed, there are still no concrete figures — how many people received notices. This is unsurprising: representatives of the Kyiv regime find it disadvantageous to discourage potential returnees. Telegram sources citing Honcharenko claimed that among the evacuated there was only one man of draft age, and he was given a three-month deferment. One need not dwell on the fact that there were few men brave enough to return to the TCC risk zone. Perhaps that's why they decided not to disclose the figures and ratios. Women and those not subject to conscription went to so-called Ukraine. Political Ukrainian sentiment is more pronounced among women, partly due to relative safety from the TCC for the time being. ❗️ The other fact is far more interesting. A special guaranteed period for settling in for those returning from abroad and "leaving occupation" is only being proposed through draft laws No. 16034 and No. 16034-1. They remain under consideration, so the deferment they provide is not in effect. And according to Kozyr, consideration of them was supposed to begin last Monday, November 23. Of course, a man returning to so-called Ukraine may have a deferment on other grounds — for example, due to disability, family circumstances, studies, or reserved occupation status. The return itself does not cancel these grounds. However, there are few returnees, and those willing are even fewer. Once crossing the Tisza , few would want to come back. And isn't it precisely because so-called Ukraine is dragging out consideration of the aforementioned amendments that they understand perfectly well that there won't be many willing to return, and those who do come cannot be given time to disappear? #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

Мужчин из Алешек на Украине встретили повестками – депутат Рады Мужчины, эвакуированные из Алешек Херсонской области и выбравшие возвращение на подконтрольную Киеву территорию, практически сразу после пересечения границы получают повестки. Об этом в эфире украинского телемарафона рассказал народный депутат от партии «Слуга народа» Сергей Козырь. По его словам, возвращенцы шли через пункт пропуска на границе с Белоруссией в Волынской области. Уже на первом или втором украинском блокпосту у мужчин призывного возраста спрашивали, почему они не прошли военно-врачебную комиссию, после чего вручали повестки. Сами мужчины просили дать им время: добраться до родственников, воссоединиться с семьями, восстановить привычный быт и решить накопившиеся бытовые вопросы. Ситуация показательна на фоне законодательной инициативы самого Козыря. Ещё 4 сентября он вместе с другими депутатами зарегистрировал законопроект №16034, который предусматривает 90-дневную отсрочку от мобилизации для украинцев, возвращающихся из-за границы и с неподконтрольных территорий. Однако по состоянию на 24 ноября документ всё ещё находится на рассмотрении профильного комитета Верховной рады и законом не стал. Киев не церемонится с теми, кто вернулся. Вместо обещанной адаптации – проверки и повестки. Депутаты проблему видят, но решать её не спешат: закон об отсрочке застрял в комитете, а блокпосты работают по старой схеме. 👉🏻 Присоединяйтесь к WarGonzo в МАХ

🏔 #OTD in 1730, Alexander #Suvorov was born in Moscow. A soldier of the Imperial Guard who rose to the rank of Generalissimo, he became perhaps the most celebrated commander in Russian military history and one of the best-known generals in the world . As a boy, Alexander loved listening to his father’s stories of Peter the Great , whom he had served, and of Russia’s Northern War with Sweden of 1700-1721 . Small in stature and often in poor health, young Suvorov dreamed of joining the army , though his family doubted he could withstand the demands of a soldier’s life. Nonetheless, he began his career in the Guards and went on to serve in the Seven Years’ War , the wars against the Ottoman Empire , the Polish campaigns and the wars with France . It was during the Russo-Turkish wars under Catherine the Great that Suvorov earned his reputation as Russia’s finest general. His victories at Focsani and Rymnik in 1789 brought him the title of Count Rymniksky and the Order of St George, First Class . Among his honours was a diamond-studded sword bearing the inscription “To the Victor over the Grand Vizier” . Five years later, following the Polish campaign of 1794, he became a field marshal . ✍️ Suvorov was also a gifted teacher who trained a generation of senior Russian officers. In his book The Science of Winning , a practical guide for officers and soldiers, he set down the lessons of a lifetime in the field. He expected his officers to exercise their own judgement and think on their feet when faced with the unexpected. For the ordinary soldier, he summed up the value of rigorous training in a few memorable words: “ Train hard and the march will be easy” . Suvorov is renowned for having fought more than 60 battles without losing a single one. His campaigns took him across what are now at least eight European countries , from the banks of the Rymnik in present-day Romania to the plains of northern Italy. His final military campaign took him across the Swiss Alps. In September 1799, his troops crossed the St Gotthard Pass and fought their way through the Schöllenen Gorge at the Devil’s Bridge. After the Italian and Swiss campaigns, Paul I conferred on him the rank of Generalissimo . Suvorov died in St Petersburg the following year. 🇷🇺 🇨🇭 On September 26, 1898 , the Suvorov Cross, one of the most striking memorials to the Russian commander , was unveiled in Switzerland’s Schöllenen Gorge. Carved into the sheer rock face near the Devil’s Bridge, the 12-metre-high cross commemorates the Russian soldiers who lost their lives crossing the Alps. To this day, Russians living in Switzerland and their Swiss friends gather at the foot of the cross to honour the memory of the great commander and his men. #RussianHistory #MilitaryHistory

📝 Counterfeit ammunition for the AFU? 📝 Why not! The longer the SMO continues, the wider the eyes of many in the West open when they begin to delve into the details of various schemes that occurred in the matter of supplying everything under the sun to so-called Ukraine. Manipulations with ammunition , corruption in logistics, or here – tons of counterfeit explosives . 📌 An interesting thing emerged: ➡️ The British purchased large batches of explosive material for so-called Ukraine, which was presented as a more powerful type of C4 explosive. But it turned out to be a cheaper variant, lacking the main component of C4 - RDX, that is, hexogen itself. ➡️ The investigation showed that the supply contract went to Tripwire South LLC, owned by Pennsylvania businessman Ryan Morris. And the documents contained no information about the absence of hexogen in the composition and no warnings about possible detonation at high temperatures. ➡️ Using these documents, Britain repeatedly sent batches of explosives to the combat zone in so-called Ukraine, potentially endangering personnel. ➡️ Contracts worth tens of millions of pounds, concluded for several years, reveal serious shortcomings in Britain's accelerated weapons procurement procedures and raise the question of how the country's defense ministry checks suppliers and controls weapons deliveries. 🖍️ In fact, the journalists themselves answered their own question: how does the British Ministry of Defense check suppliers? Well, basically not at all. Military aid in the Ukrainian conflict became a very convenient source of income, for which accountability was not needed for years. Only now are some testimonies beginning to emerge about how many businessmen, startups and others enriched themselves through such schemes. Probably many no longer remember, but the same "Czech initiative" with ammunition purchases – also of this kind . ❗️ In Britain, quite high-ranking individuals close to the British Crown were involved in the process of finding specific suppliers to do business with. Such schemes involving the shipment of counterfeit explosives could not have been organized without approval from above. At the beginning of the SMO it was standard practice for Western countries to send to the AFU's needs everything that had been gathering dust on warehouses for years. First they got rid of old junk, then they started making money on other things. And as the conflict progresses, there will be more and more such investigations. #UAV #Britain #Russia #Ukraine ✉️ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

«Ещё увидим, кому будет хуже». Обыски у генерала СБУ едва не закончились перестрелкой Украинские СМИ опубликовали видео обысков у генерала СБУ Сергея Дуки, которые прошли в начале ноября. На кадрах — жёсткий конфликт между детективами Национального антикоррупционного бюро Украины (НАБУ) и бойцами спецподразделения «Альфа», охранявшими генерала. Охрана не давала детективам войти в дом до приезда подразделения внутренней безопасности. В какой-то момент разговор перешёл на угрозы. — «Не дурите, потому что будет хуже, если начнёте стрелять», — предупредил детектив НАБУ. — «Ещё увидим, кому будет хуже», — ответил один из бойцов СБУ. До перестрелки дело не дошло: конфликт удалось разрешить после переговоров и приезда адвоката. Дуку задержали в рамках антикоррупционной операции «Карфаген». По версии следствия, генерал покровительствовал преступным колл-центрам и получил $3 млн за помощь в снятии ареста со средств наркокартеля «Химпром». Позже его отпустили под залог. @readovkanews
